functions.does: Driving (remote, one stick): two Power Functions XL motors, one on each axle, each turn their axle's pinion into its differential, and the differential drives both portal hubs, so all four wheels drive.
functions.source: book 4: function page 64 (the remote's left stick and the wheel arrows); books 2-3: axle sub-builds (steps 26, 48, 61)
functions.note: the XL motors themselves are only LDCad cable paths in the model file (step48-motor, step61-motor), so the controls named are the gears on the motors' outputs; each motor drives only its own axle

functions.does: Steering (remote, other stick): the Power Functions servo turns a shaft running front and back under the chassis; through universal joints it turns a gear on each axle's steering rack, so the front and rear wheels steer together, the rear the opposite way (four-wheel steering, crab-free).
functions.source: book 4: function page 64 (front and rear wheels both turning); book 1: steps 5 and 20 (servo and the shaft with universal joints); steps 30-33 (racks)
functions.note: the servo is only an LDCad cable path (step5-motor), so the control named is the servo's output shaft; whether the rear wheels steer opposite to the front is inferred from the photo

functions.does: Each axle is a live axle hung on the chassis with shock absorbers and links, so it can tilt and rise over rough ground (articulation).
functions.source: book 2: steps 68-72 (the shock absorber sub-builds); inferred: no motion arrows

functions.does: The shock absorbers' springs hold the chassis up on its axles.
functions.skip: the springs only push back under the model's weight

functions.does: The front winch: a Power Functions M motor, switched by hand with the pole-reverser switch behind the cab, turns a worm that drives a 24-tooth clutch gear on the winch reel, winding the hook's rope in or out; the clutch gear slips when the hook is all the way in.
functions.source: book 4: function page 65 (1: turning the switch, 2: the hook going in and out); book 2: step 40 (winch sub-build)
functions.note: the M motor and the pole-reverser switch are only LDCad cable paths (step40-1-motor, step89-polerev); the control named is the worm on the motor's shaft

functions.source: book 4: step 104 (the white arrows at the doors)

functions.does: The whole body shell tilts up on a hinge at the back, for getting at the battery box and switches, and folds back down.
functions.source: book 4: steps 103-104 (shell standing up, then the big arrow lowering it)

functions.does: The headlights (two Power Functions LEDs) light up when the battery box is switched on.
functions.source: book 4: function page 64 (lights inset); book 3: step 90
